final_candidates.decision_summary: Cys44 is a conserved RING zinc ligand; C44A has maximal LOF phenotype and rare substitution frequency, supporting strong DNA-repair disruption.
Cys24 is a conserved RING cysteine with maximal LOF phenotype and rare A substitution, making it a strong function-abolishing candidate.
Cys39 to Ala shows near-maximal LOF phenotype and low mutation plausibility at a conserved RING zinc ligand, consistent with functional knockout.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to reorder the top three RING zinc-ligand substitutions.

history.rationale: Cys61 is a RING zinc ligand essential for BRCA1/BARD1 E3 ligase activity; C61G is a known pathogenic LOF variant expected to abolish RING function while leaving most of the protein folded.
RING zinc ligand substitution expected to abolish E3 ligase/DNA-repair function, with a known pathogenic BRCA1 variant at this position.
High phenotype LOF but poor Cys->Gly sequence plausibility; ranked below C47G due to slightly lower phenotype.
Conserved RING cysteine with high LOF signal remains plausible despite lower sequence plausibility.
Cys64 is another RING zinc-coordinating residue; substitution should disrupt the zinc-binding module and E3 ligase function without necessarily unfolding the full protein.
RING zinc ligand disruption likely to impair function; prior confidence remains high.
Strong phenotype LOF but low Cys->Gly plausibility; lower confidence than top C->A choices.
Conserved RING cysteine with high LOF phenotype, though MSA coverage is reduced and Cys-to-Gly is less sequence-plausible.
Cys47 participates in RING zinc coordination; mutation likely destabilizes the RING domain and abrogates BRCA1 ubiquitin ligase activity.
RING zinc ligand disruption likely to abolish function, though folding preservation is more uncertain than for BRCT missense variants.
Phenotype LOF is very high but Cys->Gly sequence plausibility is very low, tempering confidence.
Conserved RING cysteine and high LOF phenotype support retention, though Cys-to-Gly has lower sequence plausibility than Cys-to-Ala.
Cys44 is a RING zinc ligand; alanine substitution should eliminate zinc coordination and E3 ligase activity while retaining the overall BRCA1 architecture.
RING zinc ligand substitution likely damaging to function; retained as active candidate.
Highest phenotype LOF score and the most plausible Cys->Ala substitution among RING zinc-ligand positions; retain top.
AlphaMissense LOF signal is maximal and MSA shows low A frequency at a conserved RING zinc ligand, supporting disruptive LOF.
Cys39 is a conserved RING zinc-coordinating residue; mutation is expected to impair RING folding and abolish tumor-suppressor function.
RING zinc ligand substitution likely damaging to function; retained as active candidate.
Very high phenotype LOF and acceptable Cys->Ala sequence plausibility; retain near top.
Lowest mutant frequency among Cys-to-Ala RING candidates strengthens the disruptive LOF expectation.
Cys27 contributes to the RING zinc-binding site; substitution should disrupt the RING/BARD1 interface and E3 ligase activity.
RING zinc ligand substitution likely damaging to function; retained as active candidate.
High phenotype LOF and same moderate Cys->Ala plausibility; rank just behind C39A due to slightly lower phenotype.
Conserved RING cysteine with rare A substitution and high LOF phenotype remains a strong candidate.
Cys24 is an N-terminal RING zinc ligand; mutation likely ablates RING-dependent DNA-repair signaling while preserving most of the protein.
RING zinc ligand substitution likely damaging to function; retained as active candidate.
Tied top phenotype LOF score with moderate sequence plausibility; retain top.
High LOF phenotype and conserved RING cysteine with rare A substitution support strong candidate.
His41 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the BRCA1 RING domain; alanine substitution is expected to disrupt metal binding and E3 ubiquitin ligase function.
RING zinc-coordinating histidine substitution likely damaging; retained but lower confidence due to folding uncertainty.
Near-maximal phenotype LOF but very low sequence plausibility for His->Ala zinc ligand; ranked below C->A variants.
Very rare A at a conserved RING histidine supports LOF, but lower sequence plausibility keeps it below Cys-to-Ala variants.
Met1775 is a BRCT phosphopeptide-binding pocket residue; M1775R is a known pathogenic missense that blocks BRCT ligand recognition while generally preserving BRCT folding.
Known BRCT-domain missense variant with strong prior for loss of tumor-suppressor function while likely preserving overall fold.
Phenotype LOF is much lower than RING zinc-ligand candidates and sequence plausibility is weak; drop in rank.
Lower LOF phenotype, negligible MSA applicability, and very low sequence plausibility make it inferior to RING-domain disruptions.

rejection.reason: Lower LOF phenotype, negligible MSA applicability, and very low sequence plausibility make it inferior to RING-domain disruptions.

history.rationale: Arg1699 is a key BRCT phosphate-binding residue; R1699W is a documented pathogenic variant expected to abolish BRCT-mediated repair interactions without globally unfolding BRCA1.
Canonical BRCT pathogenic missense variant likely to disrupt phosphopeptide binding and DNA repair while retaining BRCT fold.
Lowest phenotype LOF and zero sequence plausibility in the fallback; least attractive retained candidate.
Lower LOF phenotype and non-applicable MSA coverage weaken confidence relative to conserved RING candidates.

rejection.reason: Lower LOF phenotype and non-applicable MSA coverage weaken confidence relative to conserved RING candidates.
